newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures fall amid dollar concerns.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures fall amid dollar concerns.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures fell across the board on Tuesday, as the dollar looked set for further declines amid concerns over Japan's burgeoning trade surplus, traders said.
"The LME performance is not impressive and people are concerned over the dollar, which looks set for another go on the downside," said one trader.
The TOCOM benchmark April 1998 contract gave up 1.6 yen to close at 187.9 yen per kilogram, while others lost from 0.8 to 2.3 yen.
Estimated volume was 2,596 lots, up from 1,078 on Monday.
Yet traders said few participants were building up positions either way.
In London overnight, benchmark three-month aluminium fell $4 to $1,582 per tonne, with the market shrugging off relentless stock draws.

Traders said participants were worried that the metal was going to consignment stocks rather than to end-users, and that idled production was being restarted at U.S. plants. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-6179
